rules.sentence: For initial evaluation, sonographic abdominal imaging is reasonable in suspected appendicitis, even if to exclude an obstetrical cause of pain (Butala, 2010).
Appendiceal computed tomography is more sensitive and accurate than sonography to conirm suspected appendicitis (Katz, 2012; Raman, 2008).
It is generally accepted that when available, MR imaging is the preferred modality for evaluation of suspected appendicitis in pregnancy (Fig. 54-4).
MR imaging has high diagnostic yield and accuracy, and it also provides alternative diagnoses (Fonseca, 2014; Theilen, 2015).
One metaanalysis cited positive-and negativepredictive values for MR imaging of 90 and 99.5 percent, respectively (Blumenfeld, 2011).
Using a decision-analysis model, CT and MR imaging were found to be cost efective (Kasten berg, 2013).
